chunks: 1219 - Abu Ja'far al-Baqir عليه السلام said to Zurarah ibn A'yan:

“Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has obligated upon the people, from one Jumu'ah to the next, thirty-five prayers. Among them is one prayer that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has obligated in congregation, and that is the Jumu'ah prayer. He has waived it from nine: the young, the old, the insane, the traveler, the slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and one who is at the distance of two farsakhs. The recitation in it is aloud, and ghusl (ritual bath) for it is obligatory. And upon the Imam in it are two qunūt: one qunūt in the first rak'ah before ruku', and in the second rak'ah after ruku'. ”

key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath associated here with Jumu'ah
key_terms.جَمَاعَةٍ: congregation; collective performance of the prayer
key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْنِ: a distance measure of two farsakhs determining exemption
key_terms.قُنُوتَانِ: two qunūt supplications prescribed in this prayer

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from Jumu'ah prayer and what are its main rulings in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for Jumu'ah prayer, identifying it as the one weekly prayer specifically obligated in congregation among the thirty-five daily prayers between two Fridays. It also lists those exempt from attending and mentions procedural rulings including aloud recitation, ghusl (ritual bath), and the two qunūt in the prayer.
